summary:
Set 107 Session 2 replaced the tutorial that staff abandoned. The new docs/tutorials/hello-world.md is 144 lines and four steps: run `Dabbler: Try a sample project`, watch a test fail, paste one line into the AI agent the reader already has open, watch it pass. It contains no git command, no YAML, no host configuration, no branch/pull-request/CI/worktree/teammate content and no governance settings, with one sanctioned exception (the closing Full-tier sentence). The previous 448-line tutorial moved to docs/tutorials/adopt-dabbler.md with its nine video scripts (docs/tutorials/video/ -> adopt-dabbler-video/), retitled and reframed as what comes AFTER the first run, carrying one labelled note that it still holds the team workflow. Every inbound link was repaired.

THE PROSE WAS ROUTED, THE LITERALS WERE BOUND. Authoring went to a different provider (documentation, anthropic excluded), but every command, path, message and output was then substituted by the orchestrator from bundle.json and the shipped string constants rather than derived by the model -- a tutorial's literals are the one thing a reader cannot recover from. Before writing a word, the sample was rendered and walked end to end on the PyPI-PUBLISHED router 0.34.0 (not this repo's editable install): red 'Ran 2 tests / FAILED (errors=1)', the change, green 'OK', 'Hello, world!' / 'HELLO, WORLD!', and 'close_session: succeeded' with all six gates passing. That walk is s2-desk-check.md, which names what it does NOT establish so it cannot be mistaken for Session 3's stopwatch.

TWO SCOPE CORRECTIONS, both against the spec's own expectations. (1) The spec said the shipped getting-started.md.template link would need no change because the new document keeps the old filename. That confirmation FAILED: both shipped templates describe the ADOPTION content by name ('a teammate, a second module, CODEOWNERS, and monorepo CI'; the greeter/app worked example), so a resolving link is not the test. Both were repointed, dist/ rebuilt, both cold-start goldens regenerated. Folded into the staged, unpublished 0.47.0 -- no new bump. (2) The spec said to extend Set 106's 'committed literal gate'; that script lives inside a session-set folder and is referenced by no CI job, no pytest test and no npm script. It was an artifact, not a gate. Its successor was authored at repo level: ai_router/scripts/tutorial_gate.py, 67 tests, and a CI step beside drift_guard. The 106 script is left working and uninvalidated.

THE GATE IS THE STORY. Its first version passed on its first run, and falsifying it before trusting it immediately caught a real weakness: the `missingFunction: "shout"` presence check was satisfied by the slug `001-add-a-shout` containing 'shout' -- the same coincidence-satisfies-presence-check class S1's third-provider opinion found. Round 1 then caught eight more escapes the falsification set had not thought to try: an ALLOWLIST of git subcommands let `git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `git reset`, `git clean`, `git rm`, `git cherry-pick` and `git worktree` through; YAML detection only saw LABELLED fences while every fence in this tutorial is unlabelled; branching and commit instructions passed; patterns were case-sensitive, so a sentence-initial 'Commit your work first.' passed; the before/after test tallies were not both required, so a tutorial that quietly dropped the failing state would have passed; the starter line was unpinned despite an adjudication document claiming otherwise; the required closing sentence was unchecked; the tutorial's quoted UI strings were bound to nothing; and missing inputs failed OPEN with a test codifying it. All fixed. Once strengthened the gate immediately failed on this session's own work twice -- 'Creating your sample project...' lives in trySampleProject.ts, not sampleProject.ts, and the Full-tier sentence check found 0 because the sentence is reflowed across two lines.

VERIFICATION: three phased rounds. Discovery fan-out 2/2 (both calls independently found the same two defects), supplementary BEFORE remediation, then remediation-review -> VERIFIED, 0 findings, 2 fixes accepted + 1 accepted-with-modification. Three distinct blockers, all accepted, none disputed: step 4's completion commands were Windows-only while step 2 had trained the reader to expect a platform pair; the gate did not enforce its advertised contract; and GIT WAS AN UNDECLARED PREREQUISITE -- the command runs git init and the agent commits, the shipped code even has a GIT_MISSING_MESSAGE for it, yet the tutorial listed four prerequisites without git while README.md promised 'no repository, and no git commands'. That third is a true-cold-start miss (L-079-3): a reader satisfies every stated prerequisite and still cannot finish. The corrected claim ('no git commands FOR YOU TO TYPE') was propagated to all five echoes in one pass (L-065-1).

POST-VERDICT: round 3's two Minors were cheap, so they were fixed rather than carried, and NOT re-verified by a routed round (the close backstop sees them). One was a real contradiction -- the tutorial demanded an agent the reader is 'already signed in to' and then said 'You do not need an account anywhere.' The other asked the untagged-YAML detector to also catch single-line blocks; doing so immediately flagged the real document's own ```Dabbler: Try a sample project``` and ```close_session: succeeded``` fences, because a one-line 'word: value' fence is not distinguishable from configuration by shape. Half taken (mapping key plus indented scalar list), half declined with both rejected shapes now carrying NEGATIVE tests so nobody re-widens it blind.

reason.specifics: Session 3 is the set's only real acceptance test -- a timed human walk of the tutorial this session wrote, on a clean VS Code profile with a released VSIX -- plus the set-terminal close, the advisory path-aware critique and the Step 9 guidance review. It should be run by a provider that authored neither S1's code nor S2's prose, so the tutorial is read the way a stranger reads it; gpt-5-6 has now been the verifier across both sessions and was right on every substantive finding in this one, including the undeclared git prerequisite that three of my own passes missed. Effort high rather than medium: a wrong call here costs operator walk-time, which is the most expensive resource in the workflow. Second choice if the operator prefers continuity: claude / anthropic / claude-opus-5 / high. Either way S3's verification excludes whichever provider orchestrates it. S3 must STOP AND RESCHEDULE if any operator-supplied precondition in the spec is missing -- a walk on a dirty profile measures the wrong thing.

blockers: NONE BLOCKING. Recorded for the operator and for Session 3:

OPERATOR-GATED, unchanged from S1: publishing extension 0.47.0 to the Marketplace (no tag vsix-v0.47.0, no publish run). This session's two template edits FOLD INTO that staged version -- 0.47.0 has never shipped, so re-bumping would be wrong. Separately, publishing dabbler-ai-router, which still carries S1's close_session EOF fix under [Unreleased]. NOTE FOR S3: the spec requires the walk to install 'the released VSIX from S1's version bump'. That VSIX DOES NOT EXIST until the operator publishes 0.47.0. This is a hard precondition for Session 3 and it is the operator's click.

SPEC DEFECT, for Step 9 / S3: the concept-ownership table (spec + proposal v3) assigns 'custom hosts' to release-and-recovery.md, which contains NO host content -- the GitHub/Azure DevOps material lives in adopt-dabbler.md, correctly. Found by the routed duplicate-procedure review. No reader is misled (the table is an internal authoring contract published in no tutorial), so it is Minor, but the table is wrong. Correct form: 'Host-specific setup (GitHub, Azure DevOps) -> adopt-dabbler.md' and 'Releases, hotfix, rollback, raw git recovery -> release-and-recovery.md'. Not fixed here: the spec's configuration is immutable at runtime.

RESIDUAL, named not hidden: the starter line 'Start the next session of `<slug>`.' now appears in both tutorials. hello-world.md's copy is pinned by tutorial_gate against bundle.json; adopt-dabbler.md's is pinned only by the command-title check. Adjudicated Minor (s2-duplicate-procedure-adjudication.md) -- the two passages do different work, and the spec forbids changing adopt-dabbler.md in substance.

RESIDUAL, gate: a SINGLE-LINE untagged YAML fence goes undetected. Widening to catch it flagged the real tutorial's own one-line fences, because 'word: value' on one line is shape-identical to configuration. Declined deliberately; both rejected shapes carry negative tests.

RESIDUAL, cosmetic, router-side: `python -m ai_router.close_session` prints a runpy RuntimeWarning about the module being in sys.modules before execution. The reader's AI agent runs this, not the reader, and the close still succeeds. Observed on published router 0.34.0 during the desk walk. Out of this session's scope.

RESIDUAL, environment, unchanged from S1: Layer 3 (Playwright) could not run on this machine -- all 28 specs fail identically inside _electron.launch before any window opens. This session changed markdown, two templates, their regenerated fixtures, and a stdlib Python gate; nothing that can move a pixel in the webview, so L-064-12's trigger does not fire. CI's playwright-tests job is the authoritative signal. Still worth an operator look.
